title: Compose provider telemetry with the scheduler usage authority
description:
SPIDR slice 3 of 4, cut from task-8e3076177f87458f934a776eca68ba16. This is the RULES slice and the heart of the original task: the daemon-side composition of runner telemetry with the scheduler usage authority.

Hard dependencies: task-8e3076177f87458f934a776eca68ba16 (record contract) and the canonical codec slice, both DONE.

DELIVERABLE: apps/daemon/src/telemetry/provider-run-normalize.ts plus its .js bridge and provider-run-normalize.test.ts.

BEHAVIOUR:
- Import ONLY from the @moe/runner and @moe/scheduler package ROOTS via bare specifiers. A deep path into packages/** fails with TS6059; this repo has no tsconfig paths and no project references, so there is no escape hatch.
- Validate ONE raw launch-bound ClaudeTelemetryHandoff. Refuse a malformed handoff with a stable code and layer.
- Delegate EVERY usage envelope to production normalizeUsageMeasurement, IN ORIGINAL PROVIDER SEQUENCE, threading the previous accepted NormalizedMeasurement as the `prior` argument. Threading `prior` is not bookkeeping: it is what makes BUDGET_OBSERVATION_SEQUENCE_GAP, SEQUENCE_REGRESSION, IDENTITY_CONFLICT and STREAM_MISMATCH reachable at all. Passing null every time silently disables four of the ten measurement codes and no test can tell.
- COPY NONE of the authority's source/coverage matrix. If the daemon decides COMPLETE vs PARTIAL vs UNKNOWN, or picks a BUDGET_MEASUREMENT_SOURCES member itself, the authority has been duplicated.
- PRESERVE BOTH PROVENANCES SEPARATELY. The upstream ProviderTelemetryRefusal {code: ProviderTelemetryCode, layer: ProviderTelemetryLayer} and the scheduler's LayeredIssue {layer: "CONTRACT"|"MEASUREMENT", code} occupy DIFFERENT record fields. Do not flatten, translate, or invent a pass.
- UNKNOWN usage retains quantity null and the exact upstream code/layer. PARTIAL retains its measured lower bound. No client-estimated Claude cost may be persisted with source ACTUAL_BILLED.

- TRAP: `grep telemetry packages/runner/src/index.ts` returns ZERO hits and is a FALSE NEGATIVE. The surface is re-exported through `export * from "./surface/claude-surface.js"` at index.ts:162; claude-surface.ts:167-212 re-exports all three telemetry modules by name. Do not report blocked on the grep.
- normalizeUsageMeasurement(input: unknown, prior?: NormalizedMeasurement | null): MeasurementResult<NormalizedMeasurement> at packages/scheduler/src/budget/budget-measurement.ts:210. Input is a {measurement, pricebookBinding, truncated} envelope.
- ClaudeTelemetryHandoff at packages/runner/src/providers/telemetry/claude-telemetry-launch.ts:70-86.
- BUDGET_MEASUREMENT_SOURCES has SIX members: PROVIDER_REPORTED_COMPLETE, PROVIDER_REPORTED_PARTIAL, DERIVED_LIST_PRICE, SUBSCRIPTION_QUOTA, ACTUAL_BILLED, UNKNOWN.

Scope: apps/daemon/src/telemetry/provider-run-normalize.* only. Persistence belongs to the ledger slice.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner test, pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test, pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck, pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test - each leg's exit code read SEPARATELY.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
THE GOVERNOR ASKED ME TO VERIFY MY OWN CORRECTION BEFORE PROMOTION. I did, and IT HOLDS: this slice depends on the record contract ONLY, not on the canonical codec.

The reasoning, from the landed contract rather than from memory. The codec's job is `encodeProviderRunRecord` -> canonical bytes + digest, and the only field it owns on the record is `recordDigest` (contracts.ts:145). This slice produces the OTHER fields: `usage`, `usageRefusals`, `upstreamRefusal`, and the launch-derived facts copied from the handoff. Nothing here needs bytes or a digest. The consumer of the codec is the LEDGER (task-1a7ff170), which encodes the composed record and commits it. So the chain shortens by one hop and this slice was plannable as soon as slice 1 landed — which it now has, at commit 9d60091.

A CONSEQUENCE THAT MUST BE DECIDED HERE, because it is this slice's output type. `ProviderRunRecord.recordDigest` is a NON-OPTIONAL string, so a composition that returns a complete `ProviderRunRecord` would have to put SOMETHING in it — and the only honest options are a placeholder or a digest this slice is not authorised to mint. A placeholder is the worse of the two: a fake digest string sitting in a typed field reads as real to every later reader, and the codec would have to know to distrust it. So THIS SLICE RETURNS THE RECORD WITHOUT THE DIGEST — a draft type (`Omit<ProviderRunRecord, "recordDigest">` or a named alias for it) — and the ledger bridges draft -> encode -> commit. That keeps digest authority in exactly one module and means no invented digest ever exists, not even briefly. This decision must be carried into the ledger slice's plan; the codec's approved plan already tolerates it, since it treats any incoming recordDigest as overwritable.

COMPOSE, NEVER RE-DERIVE. `normalizeUsageMeasurement` is the authority and its own root doc says publishing the bare validator "would hand a consumer a gate that accepts records the authority refuses". This slice therefore makes NO coverage or source decision of its own — if the daemon ever picks a BUDGET_MEASUREMENT_SOURCES member or a coverage class, the authority has been duplicated. Task rail 1 also forbids injecting a fake normalizer in tests, which is the prohibition that created this whole family.

REJECTED: dropping refused envelopes. The contract's own comment at :62-72 explains why they are retained — "a dropped envelope and an envelope the provider never emitted are indistinguishable in the durable bytes", so a benchmark reading three accepted rows could not tell a fully measured run from one whose fourth envelope was silently discarded. `ProviderRunUsageRefusal.providerSequence` exists precisely because the scheduler's failure arm cannot carry it.

planningNotes.risks:
THREADING `prior` IS THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A REAL COMPOSITION AND A DECORATIVE ONE. `normalizeUsageMeasurement(input, prior?)` reaches SEQUENCE_GAP, SEQUENCE_REGRESSION, IDENTITY_CONFLICT and STREAM_MISMATCH only through `checkAgainstPrior`. Passing null on every call silently disables four of the ten measurement codes, the suite stays green, and nothing anywhere reports a problem. Thread the last ACCEPTED measurement — not the last envelope, since a refused envelope must not advance the chain — and prove it with an out-of-order and a duplicate-identity case that surface the scheduler's own codes.

A REFUSED ENVELOPE MUST NOT BE DROPPED, and must not advance `prior` either. Both are silent: dropping loses the distinction between a fully measured run and one with a discarded envelope (the contract comment at :62-72 says so outright), and advancing `prior` past a refusal corrupts every later sequence check. `providerSequence` on the refusal is the field that makes the first detectable — populate it from the ORIGINAL emission order, not from the surviving-rows index, or the two runs become indistinguishable again.

DO NOT MERGE THE TWO PROVENANCES. `upstreamRefusal` (the provider seam) and `usageRefusals[].issues` (the scheduler's CONTRACT/MEASUREMENT layers) are separate FIELDS in the landed contract. Merging them is not merely untidy — it is unrepresentable in the type, so a worker who tries will be tempted to flatten one into the other. Assert both codes AND both layers.

DO NOT MINT A DIGEST. `recordDigest` belongs to the codec. This slice returns the record WITHOUT it (draft type). If a placeholder digest is used instead, a fake hex string sits in a typed field and reads as real to every later reader.

SIX SOURCES, AND THE SWEEP MUST ASSERT ITS OWN CARDINALITY. Derive the expected count from the imported BUDGET_MEASUREMENT_SOURCES array, and pin the six NAMES literally. A sweep whose expectation is derived from the same array it is testing compares the array with itself and survives any addition; a sweep that generates zero cases passes while testing nothing.

THE COST CLAUSE IS A NEGATIVE PROPERTY. Feed a client-estimated cost and assert the persisted source is NOT ACTUAL_BILLED. A happy-path test never exercises the promotion the DoD forbids.
